Subject: Re: Redshifts shifted after upgrade to lumenfit 2.5.0?

Yes, I read the changelog. That is not where the disagreement is.

The 2.5.0 entry in CHANGES.md says "Refactor LineList and spectral frame handling (#812)". That is all it says. Nothing there, and nothing in the reorganised docs, tells a user that a default flipped. I did the reading, and the reading does not contain the information needed to avoid the break.

I went through the diff of PR #812 this evening. `LineList.__init__` now defaults to `wave_frame='vacuum'`; in 2.4.3 the default was `wave_frame='air'`. My slit spectra are wavelength calibrated in air from arc lamps, so every rest wavelength is now converted. The vacuum/air ratio at 6563 A is about 1.00028, which is exactly the redshift offset I reported, roughly 83 km/s, same sign and size for every object in every fit. That is not a coincidence and it is not my calibration.

Two days of this. I re-reduced the arc lamps for 40 spectra and re-ran the full reduction to find nothing wrong with my data, because there was nothing wrong with my data. Marking the thread solved also meant m_okonkwo, who reported the same offset above, got no answer to the same question.

On "works for me": if your data is already in vacuum wavelengths, or radio, then a default change to vacuum obviously makes no difference to your fits. That is consistent with this bug, not evidence against it. "Works for me" simply did not exercise the changed code path.

Workaround, so it is findable by search:

    LineList(..., wave_frame='air')

Pass wave_frame explicitly, do not rely on the default. Downgrading to 2.4.3 also works but that is not a fix.

What I am asking for:

1. Please reopen this thread.
2. An explicit line in CHANGES.md, for example "LineList default wave_frame changed from 'air' to 'vacuum' (#812)", plus a warning at runtime when wave_frame is not set explicitly.

I am annoyed, but I am only trying to get the information into the changelog so nobody else loses two days to it.
